Adjustment of status

Applying for a green card while staying in the U.S. can be easier than you think. Our immigration team in Florida helps you complete your adjustment of status with confidence and precision. Whether you’re in Miami or Orlando, we guide you step by step.

Many immigrants qualify for this process without leaving the country, avoiding consular delays. Our specialists review every form carefully to ensure your application meets USCIS requirements and moves forward smoothly.

Based near communities such as Tampa and Fort Lauderdale, our immigration experts have years of experience helping individuals and families achieve legal residency in Florida through this essential service.

What is the adjustment of status service?

The adjustment of status allows eligible immigrants already in the U.S. to become lawful permanent residents without returning to their home country. It’s one of the most direct paths to obtaining a green card legally.

Our consultants prepare all USCIS forms, verify your eligibility, and handle documentation to ensure your process runs efficiently. This service helps you remain legally in the U.S. while pursuing permanent residency.

Having experienced professionals assist you greatly reduces errors, delays, and the stress that can come from navigating complex immigration forms on your own.

What benefits do you receive by hiring this service?

Choosing our immigration office in Florida for adjustment of status ensures a smoother and more reliable path to legal residency.

  • Step-by-step guidance from start to approval
  • Detailed document review and error prevention
  • Personalized eligibility evaluation
  • Assistance with biometric and interview scheduling
  • Representation and follow-up with USCIS
  • Bilingual support in English and Spanish
  • Confidential and professional handling of your case

These benefits give you security, transparency, and peace of mind while pursuing your green card through adjustment of status.

How does the adjustment of status process work?

Understanding the process helps you prepare all requirements correctly and avoid delays in your green card application.

  1. Initial consultation to confirm eligibility and visa category
  2. Gathering all required forms and supporting evidence
  3. Submission of Form I-485 to USCIS
  4. Biometric appointment and background checks
  5. Adjustment of status interview (if required)
  6. Approval and green card issuance

Following each step properly ensures a smooth process and increases your chances of a positive outcome.

What should you know before starting your adjustment of status?

Before applying, make sure you understand eligibility requirements, forms, and timelines to prevent unnecessary delays.

Proper preparation of supporting documents and accurate form completion are crucial to avoid rejections. Our team provides full guidance to ensure compliance with all USCIS standards.

Knowing these details before applying helps you make informed decisions and keeps your path to legal residency on track.

FAQ

Here are the most common questions about adjustment of status in Florida, answered simply and directly for your convenience.

Who can apply for adjustment of status?

Immigrants who entered the U.S. legally and meet eligibility requirements for a green card category can apply for adjustment of status.

How long does the process take?

Processing times vary but usually range from 8 to 14 months, depending on USCIS workload and case complexity.

Can I work while my case is pending?

Yes, after filing your application, you can request a work permit (EAD) while your adjustment of status is being processed.

Do I need to attend an interview?

Most applicants must attend an interview at a USCIS field office to verify eligibility and confirm submitted information.

What happens if my case is denied?

You may appeal or file a new application if eligible. Professional help ensures your next submission meets all requirements.

Can I travel while waiting for approval?

Only if you have an approved advance parole document. Traveling without it may result in automatic abandonment of your case.

What documents are needed?

Form I-485, passport, I-94, photos, proof of status, medical exam, and supporting evidence such as marriage or employment records.

Is hiring an immigration attorney recommended?

Yes, an attorney or expert ensures accuracy, compliance, and smooth communication with USCIS throughout your case.

If you still have questions about adjustment of status, contact our team today for expert, personalized immigration guidance in Florida.
